explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/979: for k ≥ 2 and f_k(n) the number of solutions to n = p_1^k + ⋯ + p_k^k in primes, is limsup f_k(n) = ∞? The Lean statement: for all k ≥ 2, limsup over n of the cardinality (in ℕ∞) of the set of multisets of k primes whose k-th powers sum to n is ⊤. Counting unordered solutions (multisets) instead of ordered tuples changes counts by at most a factor k!, which does not affect whether the limsup is infinite. Faithful (positive form of the yes/no question).
